questions.question: Why do animals have adaptations?
options: To help them survive in their environment
To allow them to change their DNA structure at will
To prevent them from interacting with other species
To make them look identical to all other species

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a physical adaptation in an animal?
options: Hunting only during the coolest parts of the night
Thick fur to provide insulation in cold climates
Migrating to warmer areas during winter
Living in underground burrows to avoid heat

questions.question: Which of the following describes a behavioural adaptation in an animal?
options: Having a layer of blubber under the skin
Being nocturnal to avoid daytime heat
Having sharp claws to catch prey
Having large ears to radiate heat away

questions.question: Why is high biodiversity important for ecosystems?
options: It reduces the need for plants to photosynthesise
It ensures only one dominant species survives
It is important to maintain healthy habitats
It prevents natural environmental changes from occurring

questions.question: What is a gene pool?
options: The physical area of water where organisms reproduce
The range of DNA in a species
A database used by scientists to store genetic codes
The physical traits expressed by a single organism

questions.question: Which of the following is a way that biodiversity can be maintained?
options: Introducing invasive species to new habitats
Monoculture farming of a single crop
Conservation, protection and gene banks
Building urban developments over wild areas

questions.question: Why is sampling used to estimate animal and plant populations in an area?
options: Because it would be impossible to count them all
Because sampling changes the DNA of the organisms
Because organisms can only be identified if they are captured
Because sampling always gives a completely error-free count

questions.question: What are quadrats and what are they used to sample?
options: Circular nets used to capture flying insects
Square frames used to sample plants or slow-moving animals
Digital sensors used to measure soil temperature
Chemicals used to identify different tree species

questions.question: Why is most sampling using quadrats carried out randomly?
options: To ensure only rare species are counted
To make the fieldwork faster to complete
To avoid bias in your results
To ensure every quadrat contains the exact same number of organisms

questions.question: What is the primary function of a classification key in ecology?
options: To calculate the total biomass of a habitat
To identify different species
To randomly place quadrats in an area
To measure the flow of energy through a food chain

questions.question: Why are organisms in an ecosystem described as interdependent?
options: They are completely independent of their surroundings
They depend upon each other for the things they need to survive
They can produce their own energy without any external resources
They all belong to the exact same species

questions.question: What role do producers play for other organisms in a food chain?
options: They break down dead organic matter
They are the top predators that control populations
All organisms depend upon them to make the food that moves through food chains
They feed on primary consumers to recycle nutrients

questions.question: Why do living organisms depend upon decomposers?
options: They produce oxygen through photosynthesis
They break down dead organisms and recycle useful substances for reuse
They act as the primary consumers in all food chains
They provide physical shelter for smaller animals

questions.question: What does the term biodiversity measure?
options: The total mass of living material in an ecosystem
The rate of photosynthesis in a specific habitat
The range of living organisms
The temperature and weather patterns of an area

questions.question: Which of the following is a physical adaptation of a plant?
options: Growing towards light
Opening flowers only in the daytime
Spines to deter consumers
Releasing seeds only after a fire

questions.question: What is biomass?
options: The total number of species in an area
The mass of living material in one or more organisms
The energy lost at each trophic level
The non-living surroundings of an ecosystem

questions.question: Where is the producer always positioned in a pyramid of biomass?
options: At the very top
In the middle
At the bottom
It is excluded from the pyramid
